If Firm A also recognizes this, they might undercut. If I stay at 11 and they drop to 10, I lose significant profit. If I drop to 10 and they stay at 11, I maximize profit. If we both drop to 10, we both earn slightly less than at 11 but avoid the worst-case scenario of being undercut. Given the game theory of a finite horizon game (Nash equilibrium in the final stage), the rational move is to deviate from the agreement. A price of 10 is a strategic move to capture demand while maintaining a high margin.
